extracted.intended_audience: U.S. employers, petitioners, designated representatives, and immigration attorneys filing or advising on H-1B registrations and petitions
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory provisions governing H-1B electronic registration, weighted selection based on OEWS wage levels, petition filing requirements linked to registrations, denial grounds, and related statutory/compliance analyses (NEPA, PRA, CRA, UMRA, Executive Orders).

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial registration period timing and notice
rubrics_metrics.description: The annual initial registration period will last a minimum of 14 calendar days and will start at least 14 calendar days before the earliest date on which H-1B cap-subject petitions may be filed for a particular fiscal year. USCIS will announce the start and end dates on its website and will announce the start at least 30 calendar days in advance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USCIS will post start/end dates at www.uscis.gov for each fiscal year; minimum length 14 days; start at least 14 days before earliest filing date; start announced at least 30 calendar days in advance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection based on unique beneficiaries
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrations will be counted based on the number of unique beneficiaries who are registered; each unique beneficiary will only be counted once toward the numerical allocation projections, regardless of how many registrations were submitted for that beneficiary or how many times the beneficiary is entered in the selection pool.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USCIS will separately notify each registrant whose registration on behalf of a beneficiary has been selected. Each unique beneficiary counted once even if multiple submissions exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required information on registration (wage level, SOC, area, passport, certifications)
rubrics_metrics.description: On the registration, the registrant must select the highest OEWS wage level that the beneficiary’s proffered wage equals or exceeds for the relevant SOC code in the area(s) of intended employment and must provide the SOC code, area of intended employment, beneficiary’s valid passport or travel document information, and all other requested information and certifications as specified on the registration form and instructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If proffered wage is lower than OEWS level I but based on another legitimate source, select 'wage level I.' If beneficiary will work in multiple locations (or multiple positions if an agent), select the lowest corresponding OEWS wage level the proffered wage will equal or exceed. If proffered wage is a range, select the OEWS wage level that the lowest wage in the range will equal or exceed. Where no current OEWS data exists, select wage level using DOL prevailing wage guidance. Each beneficiary must be registered under one valid passport/travel document; when abroad, passport information must correspond to the passport intended for U.S. entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment of wage level when multiple registrations exist for one beneficiary
rubrics_metrics.description: When weighting is applied, USCIS will assign each unique beneficiary to the lowest OEWS wage level among all registrations submitted on the beneficiary’s behalf.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine lowest OEWS wage level across all registrations for that beneficiary before applying weighted entry counts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weighted selection entry counts by OEWS wage level
rubrics_metrics.description: If a random selection is necessary, USCIS will enter each unique beneficiary into the selection pool in a weighted manner: wage level IV entered four times, level III three times, level II two times, and level I one time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weighted entries increase selection probability proportionally to assigned OEWS wage level (IV=4, III=3, II=2, I=1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure if fewer unique registrations than needed for regular cap
rubrics_metrics.description: If at the end of the initial registration period USCIS determines there are fewer unique beneficiaries with properly submitted registrations than needed to meet the H-1B regular cap, USCIS will notify all petitioners with properly submitted registrations that their registrations have been selected and will keep the registration period open beyond the initial period until it receives a sufficient number of registrations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USCIS will continue accepting registrations until sufficient unique beneficiaries are properly registered to meet the regular cap; once sufficient, USCIS will stop accepting registrations under section 214(g)(1)(A). USCIS monitors unique beneficiary counts and will notify the public of the final registration date (notification timing does not control the applicable final registration date).

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure if sufficient unique registrations during initial period
rubrics_metrics.description: If at the end of the initial registration period USCIS determines there is more than a sufficient number of unique beneficiaries with properly submitted registrations to meet the H-1B regular cap, USCIS will no longer accept registrations and will notify the public of the final registration date; USCIS will weight each unique beneficiary and randomly select the number necessary to meet the cap.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USCIS will weight per OEWS wage level and perform computer-generated random selection when more unique beneficiaries exist than required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analogous procedures for H-1B advanced degree exemption (fewer/sufficient registrations)
rubrics_metrics.description: For the H-1B advanced degree exemption numerical limitation, USCIS follows analogous procedures: if fewer unique beneficiaries are properly registered than needed, notify all petitioners and continue to accept registrations until sufficient; if more than sufficient, close registrations, weight beneficiaries, and randomly select as needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitored separately for the advanced degree exemption; same weighting and selection mechanisms apply as for the regular cap.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reserve registrations and reopening registration to meet allocations
rubrics_metrics.description: Unselected properly submitted registrations for unique beneficiaries will remain on reserve for the applicable fiscal year; if USCIS needs to increase the number projected to meet allocations, USCIS will select from among reserved unique beneficiaries, and may reopen the registration period until sufficient registrations are received.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When selecting additional unique beneficiaries, USCIS will follow the weight-and-selection rules in paragraphs (h)(8)(iii)(A)(4)–(6). If reopening, USCIS will announce start of re-opened registration period on its website.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing requirement: petition must be based on a valid registration
rubrics_metrics.description: A petitioner may file an H-1B petition for a beneficiary who may be counted under the statutory caps only if the petition is based on a valid registration: properly submitted in accordance with §103.2(a)(1), paragraph (h)(8)(iii) and the registration tool instructions; submitted by the petitioner or its designated representative on behalf of the beneficiary selected for that cap season.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A petitioner may not substitute the beneficiary named in the original registration or transfer the registration to another petitioner. USCIS may, in its discretion, permit limited changes (e.g., legal name change due to marriage, passport renewal/replacement) or changes in area(s) of intended employment if consistent with bona fide job offer requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition content and evidence must match selected registration
rubrics_metrics.description: An H-1B petition filed on behalf of a beneficiary must contain and be supported by the same identifying information and position information, including SOC code, provided in the selected registration and indicated on the labor condition application, and must include a proffered wage that equals or exceeds the prevailing wage for the corresponding OEWS wage level in the registration for the SOC code in the area(s) of intended employment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitioners must submit evidence of the basis of the wage level selected on the registration as of the date the registration was submitted, and evidence of the passport/travel document used at registration. USCIS may deny or revoke petitions that do not meet these requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition-based cap-subject selection when registration process suspended
rubrics_metrics.description: If USCIS suspends the H-1B registration process for cap-subject petitions, USCIS will accept petitions and conduct a cap-subject selection based on petitions received; each petitioner must select the highest OEWS wage level that the beneficiary’s proffered wage equals or exceeds for the relevant SOC code and area(s) of intended employment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules for multiple locations, below-OEWS-I wages, and lack of OEWS data (use DOL guidance) apply. If random selection is necessary, each petition will be assigned the OEWS wage level selected and entered into the selection pool weighted (IV=4, III=3, II=2, I=1). Petitioners must submit evidence of the basis of the selected wage level as of petition submission. USCIS may deny petitions indicating exemption if found ineligible; fees will not be returned if petition denied under this paragraph.

rubrics_metrics.name: H-1B regular cap selection procedures when registration suspended (final receipt date and first five business days)
rubrics_metrics.description: When determining whether enough cap-subject petitions exist to meet the regular cap, USCIS will consider all properly submitted petitions and historical data; it will announce the date it receives the number projected as needed (final receipt date). If that final receipt date is any of the first five business days petitions may be received, USCIS will weight each petition and randomly select among petitions properly submitted during those first five business days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USCIS uses historical data related to approvals, denials, revocations, and other factors when projecting needed petition counts. Announcement timing does not control the final receipt date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advanced degree exemption selection procedures when registration suspended
rubrics_metrics.description: After completing regular cap processing, USCIS will determine if sufficient remaining petitions exist to meet the advanced degree exemption numerical limitation; it will announce a final receipt date and (if that date is any of the first five business days) will weight and randomly select petitions from those first five business days as necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Same weighting and selection approach applies as for the regular cap in suspended-registration scenarios.

rubrics_metrics.name: Denial for inaccurate, fraudulent, or materially misrepresented statements
rubrics_metrics.description: The petition will be denied if it is determined that statements on the petition, the H-1B registration (if applicable), the temporary labor certification, or the labor condition application were inaccurate, fraudulent, or misrepresented a material fact, including if certifications on the registration are false.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An H-1B cap-subject petition will also be denied if not based on a valid registration submitted by the petitioner (or designated representative) or successor in interest for the beneficiary named or identified in the petition. A valid registration must represent a bona fide job offer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Denial for attempts to unfairly increase chance of selection (gaming)
rubrics_metrics.description: USCIS may deny a subsequent new or amended petition filed by the petitioner, or a related entity, on behalf of the same beneficiary if USCIS determines the filing is part of an attempt to unfairly increase the chance of selection during registration or petition selection, such as changing the proffered wage in a subsequent new or amended petition to an amount equivalent to a lower wage level than indicated on the registration or the original cap-subject petition if registration suspended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example anti-pattern: changing the proffered wage in a later filing to an amount that would be equivalent to a lower OEWS wage level than on the original registration to try to manipulate selection probability.

rubrics_metrics.name: NEPA categorical exclusion criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Under DHS NEPA implementing procedures, for an action to be categorically excluded it must satisfy three conditions: (1) the entire action clearly fits within one or more categorical exclusions; (2) the action is not a piece of a larger action; and (3) no extraordinary circumstances exist that create the potential for a significant environmental effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS found this final rule fits categorical exclusion A3 (administrative change with no change in environmental effect), is not part of a larger action, and does not present extraordinary circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paperwork Reduction Act (PRA) submission requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the PRA, DHS must submit to OMB for review and approval any reporting requirements inherent in a rule unless they are exempt; the information collection notice was published in the Federal Register to obtain comments regarding proposed edits to the information collection instruments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific information collection instruments (H-1B Registration Tool OMB No. 1615-0144; Form I-129 OMB No. 1615-0009) are listed with type, affected public, estimates of respondents, hour burdens, and total annual cost/hour burdens as part of PRA compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information collection details for H-1B Registration Tool and Form I-129
rubrics_metrics.description: H-1B Registration Tool (OMB 1615-0144) is a revision of a currently approved collection primarily affecting businesses; Form I-129 (OMB 1615-0009) is a revision of a currently approved collection with detailed respondent and hour burden estimates for multiple supplements and filing modes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final rule provides estimated respondent counts and average hour burdens (e.g., registration tool respondents and hour burden per response 0.9333 hours; I-129 paper filing respondents 527,606 with 2.55 hour burden; total estimated annual hour burdens and total annual cost burden for Form I-129 provided). These figures support PRA analysis and compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Congressional Review Act (CRA) major rule determination and delayed effective date
rubrics_metrics.description: OIRA has determined that this final rule is a major rule as defined in 5 U.S.C. 804, and therefore the rule requires at least a 60-day delayed effective date; DHS has complied with CRA reporting requirements and sent the final rule to Congress and the Comptroller General as required by 5 U.S.C. 801(a)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Major rule designation triggers CRA procedural requirements including delayed effective date and transmittal to Congress and GAO.

rubrics_metrics.name: UMRA applicability determination
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the Unfunded Mandates Reform Act (UMRA) Title II, agencies must prepare a written statement assessing effects of any Federal mandate resulting in $100 million (1995 dollars) or more in any one year; DHS determined this final rule does not contain a Federal mandate as defined under UMRA and therefore Title II requirements do not apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DHS uses inflation-adjusted thresholds (e.g., $100M in 1995 ≈ $206M in 2024) when assessing UMRA applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive Order compliance determinations (Federalism, Civil Justice Reform, Tribal Consultation)
rubrics_metrics.description: DHS determined under E.O. 13132 that the final rule will not have substantial direct effects on the States and thus no federalism summary impact statement is warranted; under E.O. 12988 the rule was drafted to provide a clear legal standard and eliminate drafting errors and ambiguities; under E.O. 13175 the rule does not have 'tribal implications' and requires no further action or analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These determinations document the agency's assessment of federalism, civil justice reform, and tribal implications and assert the rule meets applicable standards in those Executive Orders.
